context: The check re-executes the returned statement against financial.sqlite and compares its rows to the gold's as a multiset (suite/families/text2sql.py:146), order-insensitive, floats to two decimals. The prompt says to return the query text, not a computed value (suite/families/text2sql.py:116). The knowing floor is one shell call (suite/families/text2sql.py:96): write the query from the card, run it once, return it.
counterfactual: The overshoot is discovery before composition: a first call on .schema and a second on SELECT DISTINCT, as the prompt at suite/families/text2sql.py:113 invites, leaves the strict pass (suite/families/text2sql.py:96) with no call to run its query and the slack pass with one. The opposite overshoot is returning the rows or a formatted answer instead of the statement, which the check at suite/families/text2sql.py:153 fails before any row is compared; and a second run on a query that already executed is a spent call that buys nothing.
decision: Answer a financial.sqlite question in one shell call: compose the complete SELECT from the schema card and the evidence, run it exactly once with sqlite3 financial.sqlite "<SELECT>" to see that it executes and the rows look plausible, then return the SELECT text as result - never the rows, never a number. Shapes the grader turns on: highest/lowest/oldest/top N is ORDER BY <col> [DESC] LIMIT N (LIMIT 1 for a superlative), not a MAX/MIN subquery; return only the columns the question asks for (a how-many question returns one COUNT, a percentage one number, 'list the account ID, district name and region' three columns in that order); COUNT(T.col) over the joined rows, COUNT(DISTINCT ...) only when the counted entity is coarser than the row (districts counted across clients); GROUP BY the entity's id when listing per-entity counts; ORDER BY matters only under LIMIT since rows compare as a multiset; one statement, no trailing scratch queries, no ROUND. Under text2sql-strict the one call is the budget; under text2sql the remaining two calls are for a repair only when the run errored.

residue: whether the rows the one run showed were plausible is judgment; the floor checks shape only
the column-order rule is only as good as the question's wording

not_this: a question over a database other than financial.sqlite, whose schema this card does not describe
a task that creates, alters or writes to the database (DDL or DML) rather than reading it with a SELECT
a shell task with no SQLite database in the working directory

lifecycle.consumer: the working pass, at boot, on a matching work-shape
lifecycle.moot_when: the families stop grading by re-execution, or the budget rises above the knowing floor by more than the slack

options.name: A — compose from the card, run once to verify, return the statement
options.why: one call fits both budgets and the run catches a syntax or column error before it reaches the grader

options.name: B — explore the schema and values first, then iterate on the query
options.why: spends the strict budget on discovery the store already holds, and in text2sql leaves at most one repair

options.name: C — return the rows the query produced
options.why: the check runs a SELECT; a number or a list is not a statement and fails before any comparison

summary.latch: a question over financial.sqlite under a shell-call budget where the result is the SELECT statement itself, not the rows it returns
not_this: a question over a database other than financial.sqlite, whose schema this card does not describe
a task that creates, alters or writes to the database (DDL or DML) rather than reading it with a SELECT
a shell task with no SQLite database in the working directory
summary.stakes: under text2sql-strict the single shell call is the whole budget; a pass that explores first has nothing left to run its query, and a pass that returns the rows instead of the statement fails the check outright
